title: Practise Now 7
summary: Use one right triangle for AC, then net South/West displacement for AE.
alt: Practise Now 7: A ship sails South 12 km (A→B), East 17 km (B→C), South 18 km (C→D), West 38 km (D→E). Find AC and AE.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A ship sails **South** from **A** to **B** (**AB = 12 km**), **East** to **C** (**BC = 17 km**), **South** to **D** (**CD = 18 km**), then **West** to **E** (**DE = 38 km**). Find the shortest distance between (i) **A and C**, (ii) **A and E**.

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔABC, **∠B = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **AC**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. South (AB) and East (BC) are perpendicular, so ∠B = 90°.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{12^2} + \role{legB}{17^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square and add
steps.narration: Square each number, then add them.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{12^2} + \role{legB}{17^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{144} + \role{legB}{289} \\ &= \role{hyp}{433}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 433 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AC^2} &= \role{legA}{AB^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{12^2} + \role{legB}{17^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{144} + \role{legB}{289} \\ &= \role{hyp}{433} \\ \role{hyp}{AC} &= \sqrt{433} = \role{ans}{20.8\ \text{km}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Net displacement of E from A
steps.narration: Add up how far **E** is South and West of **A** overall.\[\begin{aligned}\text{South} &: AB + CD = 12 + 18 = \role{legB}{30}\ \text{km} \\ \text{West} &: DE - BC = 38 - 17 = \role{legA}{21}\ \text{km}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Apply Pythagoras for AE
steps.narration: **A** and **E** are the ends of a right angle between the 30 km South and 21 km West legs.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AE^2} &= \role{legB}{30^2} + \role{legA}{21^2} \\ &= 900 + 441 = 1341 \\ \role{ans}{AE} &= \sqrt{1341} = \role{ans}{36.6\ \text{km}}\quad(\text{3 s.f.})\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check AC
challenges.prompt: Find **AC** when **AB = 12 km** South and **BC = 17 km** East, **∠B = 90°**.

takeaways: Track **net displacement**: add South legs, add North legs, then subtract to get the overall South (or North) distance; do the same for East–West.
The overall South and East displacements are **perpendicular**, so Pythagoras gives the straight-line distance.

notes.title: Net displacement
notes.text: The straight-line distance from start to finish depends only on the **total** South–North and East–West movement, not the path taken.
